newsitem.title: TAIWAN: China Airlines seeks syndicated loans.
newsitem.headline: China Airlines seeks syndicated loans.

text.p: Taiwan carrier China Airlines said on Wednesday it had sought around US$320 million in syndicated loans from local and foreign banks to finance its ambitious fleet expansion plan.

"Our financial department has sent out inquiries to domestic and foreign banks in Taiwan, asking for a syndicated loan from these institutions to finance our project," airline spokesman Steve Yang told Reuters.
He said the banks were expected to send back their responses, and China Airlines would then decide the loan's exact amount.
"The amount we plan to borrow is not fixed yet, but could be somewhere around US$320 million as some news media have reported," Yang said.
Company officials said under the plan China Airlines would buy 24 new planes by the end of 2003, taking the size of its fleet to 67.
Between 1997 and 1998, the company would import 17 planes, which would cost about T$18.39 billion, they added.
Yang said the company issued T$3.5 billion worth of seven-year convertible bonds in 1996, and in early 1977 applied for a capital increase of T$6 billion.
Delivery of the first two planes is expected between May and September, and the rest would be delivered by the end of December 1998, he added.
